### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **79** documentable anchor(s).

**44** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c7cfbf0a962ad690f1b4cbe271c95d909000d64`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `logError (9 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 38 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- **18** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c7cfbf0a962ad690f1b4cbe271c95d909000d64` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c1315fc943e8ace4d8f6bd74d97794c2042f85e8` — the merge of head `8c7ee7f06aaf4cc75d3a1b2536a2ac18196de4dd` into base `9c7cfbf0a962ad690f1b4cbe271c95d909000d64`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c1315fc943e8ace4d8f6bd74d97794c2042f85e8 && git checkout c1315fc943e8ace4d8f6bd74d97794c2042f85e8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9c7cfbf0a962ad690f1b4cbe271c95d909000d64 8c7ee7f06aaf4cc75d3a1b2536a2ac18196de4dd && git checkout -B drift-repro 9c7cfbf0a962ad690f1b4cbe271c95d909000d64 && git merge --no-ff 8c7ee7f06aaf4cc75d3a1b2536a2ac18196de4dd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c7cfbf0a962ad690f1b4cbe271c95d909000d64
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9c7cfbf0a962ad690f1b4cbe271c95d909000d64` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8c7ee7f06aaf4cc75d3a1b2536a2ac18196de4dd`
Local-runs: none

PR #23302 (#22975 slice 7b, re-cut) on branch `claude/issue-22975-7b-recut`, base `main`. The head's merge-base with `origin/main` is `9c7cfbf0a9`, which IS the current `origin/main`, so the merge ref `c1315fc943` carries the head's tree unchanged (zero-line diff between the two). Three-dot diff: 12 files, +74 / -1,338 = 1,412 changed lines, under 3,000. Inputs read: the card body, comments 6120370976, 6124054616, 6148409420, 6150584500, 6150594560 and 6150657199, the PR body and file list, the net diff, S8's squash `66949b7729` (#23222), ADR-0131 and ADR-0087 on `origin/main`, and the head's check-runs. The body opens `Refs #22975` then `Clause-②: no`; no closing keyword in the body or in the three commits.

### ① Derived judgments

**Dead before deletion — yes, every symbol, measured on `origin/main` across the whole tree (every package, examples and scripts).**
- `position-write-through.ts`: the only importers on `main` are `catalog-reference-report.ts` (`POSITION_OBJECT`, `metadataDoorAcceptsPositionName`; this PR removes the import) and `position-environment-backfill.ts` (deleted here). S8's own diff on `security-plugin.ts` removed the `createPositionWriteThrough` import and its `sys_position` registration, so the middleware has had no caller since `66949b7729`. No other file names `createPositionWriteThrough`, `packageHoldsPosition`, `isPositionMetadataDoor`, `positionBodyFromRow` or `POSITION_METADATA_TYPE`.
- `position-environment-backfill.ts`: no importer on `main`. S8 removed the `runOneTimePositionEnvironmentBackfill` import and the `kernel:bootstrapped` hook that ran it. No file names any of its exports.
- `PositionNameConflictError` (`errors.ts`): its only thrower was the write-through; the only other mention is the `FLOOR` list in `errors.test.ts`, which this PR trims. The class is a non-exported sibling of the retained `PermissionSetNameConflictError` and stamps that class's constants, so no code or status spelling leaves with it.
- The report's categories 4 and 5 were already inert on `main`: `collectCatalogReferences` reads `sys_position` only when `engine.getObject('sys_position')` answers, and after S8 nothing on `main` registers that object outside the test kit `__tests__/legacy-catalog-objects.testkit.ts`. The report already listed `sys_position` under `absent` on a post-S8 boot.
- The objectui pinned sibling (`.objectui-sha` `1fb1ced362`) is NOT checked out in this container and is NOT MEASURED. Structurally it cannot be affected: see the package entry below.

**The package entry — no deleted symbol was ever reachable from it.** `src/index.ts` on `main` re-exports nothing from `position-write-through.js`, `position-environment-backfill.js` or `catalog-reference-report.js`, and from `errors.js` only `PermissionDeniedError` and `isPermissionDeniedError`. `package.json` publishes one export, `.` (no subpaths), so a deep import cannot reach the deleted modules either. The PR does not touch `index.ts` or `package.json`. Therefore no ADR-0087 `runtime-export-retired` entry and no FROM → TO are owed, and the changeset's `patch` with no marker is the correct shape. This corrects the claim 6120370976's expectation that 7b "retires `plugin-security` exports": measured, 7b retires none; that expectation holds for 7a only.

**The reference report (`catalog-reference-report.ts`).** Categories 4 and 5 are dropped as one unit: the `readPositions` scan, the two `logError` blocks, the `posture` input (`CatalogReferenceReportDeps.posture`, `CatalogReferenceReport.posture`), the `PositionWithoutDefinition` and `ConflictingPositionName` interfaces, the `positionsWithoutDefinition` bucket field and the `conflictingPositionNames` top-level field, the `postureEnforcesWall` import, and the `sys_position` entry of `absent`. The only two consumers of `posture` were those categories; `security-plugin.ts` stops passing `this.tenancyPosture`. Categories 1–3 (unresolved assignments, unresolved grants, unnamed grants) are untouched line for line: the assignment and grant blocks, `scanAll`, `catalogResolver`, the `ReportStop` handling and `perOrganization` are not in the diff. The clean-boot `info` line changes text (drops "and no position row is without a definition") and its guard on `absent.length` goes from "fewer than three" to "fewer than two", the same meaning over two objects instead of three. Tests: 12 `it` blocks on `main`, 9 on the head; the three removed pin only the dropped categories (walled positions without definition, a walled position leaving the report after a door save, and conflicting names under `single`). The positive half of the second one — a position saved through the metadata door resolves in the catalog and is not reported — survives in the first test (`s3_env_lead` saved via `saveMetaItem`, then an assignment to it, `findings` empty). The remaining tests lose only the dropped fields and the `absent` entry. No doc, README, message or test on the head still names the two dropped lines; the two surviving comments (`catalog-reference-report.test.ts:437`, `grant-permission-set-name-backfill.test.ts:679`) say the backfill ran "until C3 stage 8 unwired it", which stays true. The `seedHolder` helper still inserts a `sys_position` row and a junction row as a deliberate control that a leftover row keeps nothing alive; that is a control, not dead setup.

**Behaviour a deployment loses — each already unreachable after S8; no guarantee leaves without a door-side home.**
1. The Setup-create / rename-into refusal `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION` (`PositionNameConflictError`) for a name the environment catalog already holds. It answered a `sys_position` data-door write; after S8 that object is not registered and the middleware is not wired, so no request could reach it. On the metadata door the uniqueness is structural rather than a refusal: one name is one environment item (`PUT /api/v1/meta/position/:name` over an existing name is an edit, never a second holder), a package-held or built-in name is refused by the door's own `packagedBaseRefusal` (`403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`; `position` takes no environment overlay), and a code/environment collision is refused at boot with `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`. The write-through's module note itself describes the 409 as the row-side mirror of those door rules.
2. The position name rule (`metadataDoorAcceptsPositionName`) was a derived mirror of the door's own two checks, `METADATA_ITEM_NAME_PATTERN` enforced at `saveMetaItem` (`protocol.ts` around line 20480) and `PositionSchema.name`; both stay on the door.
3. The two boot report lines (categories 4 and 5) and the walled-posture remedy text: unreachable since S8 as shown above. Legacy rows are the upgrade ceremony's (ADR-0131 D10, fates 2 and 4), which this PR's changeset says.
4. The one-time backfill and its `sys_migration` verdict row `adr-0131-position-environment-backfill`: unregistered by S8; existing verdict rows stay inert, with no reader left on the head.
5. The one observable delta on a post-S8 deployment: `absent` no longer lists `sys_position`, and the clean-boot `info` line is shorter. Neither is a published surface.

**Regenerated files — consistent with the diff.** The census script loses the write-through's `UNTYPED_RECEIVERS` row (2 sites: `delete`, `update` on `sys_position`), and the backfill's one readable-receiver `insert` goes with its file: 228 → 225 sites, `UNTYPED_RECEIVERS` 8 → 6, readable receiver 186 → 185, `any` receivers 42 → 40, `const`-named 52 → 50, decidable 155 → 153, runtime-named 73 → 72, elevated 123 → 120, threading a tenant context 167 → 164; the counts file drops exactly the three rows. Row 11b leaves `system-context.mdx`; no other page cites 11b. CI's `check-tenant-audit-census` and `check-system-context-census` (in `lint.yml`) are green on this head. The "Measured on" stamp reads `66949b772`, the regeneration base rather than the head; the page's own rule is that the corpus-scale figures say when they were true and are not compared, so this is permitted, and the dev re-ran both checks on `8c7ee7f06a`.

**Published text.** Corrected here: `system-context.mdx` row 11b, the report's module JSDoc, the write-through JSDoc in `errors.ts` (deleted with the class), the changeset's own account. No ADR names either module or any of their functions, so no governed text goes false. Not corrected and not carried by name: `packages/core/src/security/position-row-definition.ts` lines 15–16 still say the mapping is what "the security plugin's row-only position backfill applies today (`positionBodyFromRow`, beside its position write-through)". After this PR that sentence is false and `positionBodyFromRow` no longer exists. `packages/core/src/security/` is read-only for this card (claim 6120370976), so the fix is not 7b's to make; it must be carried by name (③).

**The deletion clause.** No test file is deleted. The three deleted `it` blocks pin only code this PR deletes, and the one assertion with a live half is pinned at the same layer in the same file. The `FLOOR` entry in `errors.test.ts` is the enumeration floor of a class that leaves; the floor is a lower bound, so trimming it with the class is the clause's "together with the code it pins". Clause satisfied.

### ② Semver level

The changeset grades `@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch` and the body declares `Clause-②: no`. Against WHICH LEVEL in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`: a `fix(` that changes no public surface stays `patch`; `minor` is for an additive widening of a published surface. Measured: the entry exports no deleted symbol, `package.json` has no subpath, `CatalogReferenceReport`'s narrowed shape is internal, and nothing widens. No narrowing or removal is hidden: the removals a deployment can observe (the 409, the report lines, the backfill) were taken out of reach by S8, whose changeset `15204-s8-catalog-row-objects-retired.md` declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and carries the ADR-0087 semantic entry `catalog-row-objects-retired`. `check-changeset-no-major` and the ADR-0087 registration step stand down on `no` + `patch`, and both passed in CI (Check Changeset: success). The PR title says `refactor(` while the changeset says `fix(`; the act, not the type, sets the level, and neither type raises it. Level upheld: `patch`, `Clause-②: no`.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev deviation, accepted:** the derived sweep (114/114), dogfood (254 files, 2,106 tests) and the CLI integration tier (119 files, 1,036 tests) were measured on `05dee10c89`, one merge of `main` before the head. Verified: `05dee10c89..8c7ee7f06a` is 51 files from `main` (spec/ui, cli, three changesets, the engine-double pin), none in `plugin-security`, the censuses or the docs pages here. The plugin-security suite, typecheck and both census checks were re-run on the head.
2. **Dev deviation, no bearing:** a mis-spelled first full build (turbo flag forwarded); re-run 74/74.
3. **7a overlap and the 7a blocker:** 7b shares `security-plugin.ts`, the census page and script, `system-context.mdx` and the counts file with 7a. 7b lands first (7a is blocked on the C measurement, 6150657199); 7a's re-cut must then merge `main` and regenerate. 7b has no code dependency on 7a or on its blocker: it deletes nothing live, and the echo hazard concerns the permission-set projector, which 7b does not touch. Judged independent.
4. **Out-of-scope observation, escalate to the C measurement:** the 7a blocker's premise (`applyRegistryWriteThrough` hydrates no stored row into the engine registry on a kernel with an `environmentId`) is stated type-agnostically, while 7b's changeset asserts "A position is written through the metadata door alone". Whether a position saved through the door resolves in the catalog on a real environment kernel is the same open fact for positions as for permission sets. NOT MEASURED here (read-only; no booted stack). Suggest C step 1 include one position saved through the door, since that is cheap and settles the sentence 7b publishes.
5. **Residue the PR leaves in gate vocabularies, carry by name or fix here:** `scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs:416` and `scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs:334` still list `persistPositionBackfillRecord`, a private function of the deleted backfill. The durability gate's own header calls a name in a Map that no seam consumes the "declared ≠ enforced" shape it rejects, but only `FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES` carries the staleness check, so this leaves no red (Lint is green). Two one-line deletions in `scripts/`, the surface this PR already edits; otherwise the 8-post dispatch must name both lines, since the "comment sweep" it carries does not cover gate vocabularies.
6. **Published JSDoc made false, carry by name:** `packages/core/src/security/position-row-definition.ts:15-16` (①). Core is read-only for this card; name it in the 8-post dispatch or on the C7b card that owns the core mappers.
7. **Not this PR's, already 8-post's by the card:** `delegated-admin-gate.ts:1330`, `security-plugin.ts:6782` and `:7075` still read or match `sys_position` rows (the delegated-admin catalog cases and the system-row gates the card assigns to 8-post).
8. **Check-runs on the head** (read at 2026-10-13T17:05Z): 32 success, 5 skipped, 3 still running. Still running: Test Core (2/6), Test Core (3/6), Test Core (4/6). Skipped by path filter: Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke. The dev's "CI's Console Pin Gate covers it" is therefore not true on this head; the console is covered structurally instead (no entry export moves, no subpath exists). Green includes TypeScript Type Check, Type Check · workspace, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the single-writer and card-claim guards, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core (5/6), Test Core (6/6). The seat reads the three shards before the queue.
9. **NOT MEASURED:** the objectui pinned sibling's imports (not checked out here); `check:platform-checklist`'s 8 reds as pre-existing (the dev's diff of the red lists against `bae5841bce` is the evidence, not repeated); `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (dev: exit 0 on 74/74; not repeated).

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-13T17:08Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript. The reviewer made reads, `git fetch` into review refs, `git grep`, REST GETs, and record writes only. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate. The seat takes the verdict as PASS. The seat queues the PR only after the two Test Core shards still running at adoption are green. The findings are carried:
- **Finding 2** (`persistPositionBackfillRecord` still listed at `scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs:416` and `scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs:334`) goes to 8-post's dispatch by name. It produces no red, so it is not worth a re-run here.
- **Finding 3** (the JSDoc of `packages/core/src/security/position-row-definition.ts:15-16` names the deleted backfill) also goes to 8-post by name.
- **Finding 4** (also measure a position saved through the metadata door on an environment kernel) is added to 7a's C measurement.
- **Finding 6** (7a merges `main` after 7b and regenerates the shared census files with the repo's tools) is already in the dispatch 6148409420.
- **Findings 1 and 5** are noted: the objectui sibling is NOT MEASURED, and no ADR-0087 marker is owed for 7b.
